blocks.text: I'll be honest: parking at Bondi on a sunny weekend can test your patience like nothing else. But after years of doing it, I've got a system - where to leave the car for free, when to just pay for the closest station, and the one move that beats the whole lottery. Here it is.

items.label: Free parking
items.value: Residential streets north of Blair St

blocks.title: Read the sign before you walk off
blocks.text: Inspectors patrol Bondi constantly and the fines are steep. Never block a driveway, and always check the sign for time limits and permit zones - a 'permit holders only' block will catch you out even when there's a clear space.

My go-to is the residential streets north of Blair Street, back from the beach: much of it is free and unrestricted, roughly a 5–7 minute walk down to the sand, and the trick is to keep heading north until the restriction signs stop. It is worth doing properly, so it has its own guide - [free parking at Bondi Beach](/bondi-blog/2023/10/4/finding-free-parking-at-bondi-beach-made-easy) covers exactly how far back to go, which streets fall inside the resident permit scheme, what time to arrive on a weekend, and when the beachfront itself becomes free.

items: Queen Elizabeth Drive car park - the council station directly behind the beach, and the largest beachfront option. It's metered daily (check Waverley Council for current hours and rates) and fills fast on a nice day.
Pacific Bondi car park - beneath the complex on Campbell Parade near the Pavilion, a short walk to the sand and open long hours daily. Pre-booking online is often cheaper than the drive-up rate.
The Hub (Hall Street) car park - often overlooked, on the pricier side, but a reliable fallback for an hour or two on a hectic day.
Street meters along Campbell Parade and the shops - handy but the dearest per hour, and time-limited.

blocks.text: All of the council bays are pay-by-plate, so there's no paper ticket to display - and the meters run 7am to 7pm, seven days. If you want the detail on how the payment apps work, what the permits cost and how the rates change through summer, that is all on [what parking at Bondi actually costs](/bondi-blog/2025/4/25/ultimate-bondi-beach-parking-guide-free-and-paid-options-for-busy-days).

Read the closest sign every single time, even if the car in front of you is parked there. Time limits, permit zones and no-stopping lines change street by street in Bondi, and inspectors patrol hard on weekends. Blocking a driveway is one of the costliest tickets you can collect - never worth it for a five-minute dash.

If you're down here often, a Waverley Council beach parking permit lets you stay unlimited time in the eligible metered beach bays - a genuinely good deal for regulars and worth checking your eligibility for with the council.

blocks.title: What it costs
blocks.text: Beach-adjacent meters are the dearest and get cheaper the further back you go. Council adjusts these rates periodically, so check Waverley Council's current parking fees rather than trusting any fixed figure - including mine.

There are designated accessible bays around the beachfront, including near Queen Elizabeth Drive and the Bondi Pavilion, and a valid Mobility Parking Scheme permit gives concessions on time limits in metered and timed bays. Exact bay locations and any current works can change, so confirm on the council's parking page or with the Pavilion before relying on a specific spot.
The move that beats the lottery

On a perfect summer's day, I skip the circling entirely: train to Bondi Junction, then the 333 or 380 bus straight down to Campbell Parade - about a 10–13 minute run. You'll be on the sand while everyone else is still hunting for a bay. If you must drive on a busy day, try the quieter blocks toward the south end, or the streets back from the Beach Road Hotel; most people aim for the middle of the beach, so the edges can be surprisingly lucky.

items.q: Is it easier to park at the north or south end of Bondi?
items.a: The south end, more often than people expect. Almost everyone aims for the middle of the beach and the North Bondi streets, so the blocks back from the southern end and around the Beach Road Hotel can still have room when the north is picked clean. It is a slightly longer walk to the main stretch of sand, and a shorter one to Icebergs.

items.q: What's the closest car park to Bondi Beach?
items.a: The Queen Elizabeth Drive car park, the council station right behind the sand and the largest beachfront option. It's metered daily and fills quickly, so arrive early and check Waverley Council for current hours and rates.

items.q: Can I get to Bondi without driving?
items.a: Easily. Take the train to Bondi Junction, then the 333 or 380 bus down to Campbell Parade - around 10–13 minutes and no parking stress at all.
